author: veelenga
body:
## Overview

This PR adds optional SMTP forwarding functionality to the LocalStack SES email viewer, allowing emails to be automatically forwarded to external SMTP servers like Mailpit.

## What's Changed

### New Features
- ✨ Optional SMTP forwarding to external servers (disabled by default)
- 🔧 Configurable via environment variables
- 🔄 Automatic duplicate detection (tracks processed message IDs)
- 📦 Clean modular architecture with dedicated `SMTPForwarder` class
- ✅ Comprehensive test coverage (15 new tests)

### Files Added
- `lib/smtp-forwarder.js` - SMTP forwarding logic
- `test/smtp-forwarder.test.js` - Test suite

### Files Modified
- `app.js` - Simplified to use new SMTPForwarder module
- `package.json` - Added nodemailer dependency
- `README.md` - Added configuration docs and examples

## Configuration

New environment variables:

| Variable | Description | Default |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| `SMTP_FORWARD_ENABLED` | Enable SMTP forwarding | `false` |
| `SMTP_FORWARD_HOST` | SMTP server hostname | `mailpit` |
| `SMTP_FORWARD_PORT` | SMTP server port | `1025` |

## Use Cases

This feature enables:
- Using modern email testing tools like [Mailpit](https://github.com/axllent/mailpit) alongside the viewer
- Dual interface: SES viewer at :3005 + Mailpit at :8025
- Testing without LocalStack Pro SMTP features
- Integrating with existing email testing workflows

## Example Setup

```yaml
services:
  localstack-aws-ses-email-viewer:
    build: .
    environment:
      - SMTP_FORWARD_ENABLED=true
      - SMTP_FORWARD_HOST=mailpit
      - SMTP_FORWARD_PORT=1025
    depends_on:
      - localstack
      - mailpit

  mailpit:
    image: axllent/mailpit:latest
    ports:
      - "8025:8025"
      - "1025:1025"
```

## Testing

All new tests pass:
```
PASS test/smtp-forwarder.test.js
  ✓ 15 tests passed
```

Tests cover:
- Configuration and initialization
- Message forwarding logic
- Recipient extraction
- Error handling
- Duplicate detection

## Breaking Changes

None - feature is opt-in and disabled by default.

## Related

This addresses the need for using Mailpit with LocalStack SES without requiring the separate email-bridge service discussed in the veer-api repo.

Contributes to #85.

## Problem
When users enable email reports or change their frequency (daily/weekly), they immediately receive an unwanted email report. This happens because the `lastReportSent` field is either null or too old, making them eligible for an immediate report in the next cron job.

## Solution
Update the preferences API to set `lastReportSent` to the current time when:
- User enables reports (changes from `false` to `true`)
- User changes frequency while reports are enabled

This ensures users receive their first report after the full interval (24 hours for daily, 7 days for weekly).

## Changes
- Fetch current user preferences before updating
- Check if `lastReportSent` should be updated based on preference changes
- Set `lastReportSent` to prevent immediate email sending
- Fix language cookie comparison bug (was comparing with session object)
- Use proper TypeScript typing with `Prisma.UserUpdateInput`

# Overview
We want track every single repo in backstage. Currently only repos with an `launch` directory i.e applications are tracked in backstage which this PR aims to change.

To track non applications repo we are adding a catalog-info.yaml file. In this PR I am adding that file via a microplane script so it 
- sets type to "unknown". In 2026 we will do an EWI to update all repos to have a type like "library", "cli", "docs", etc
- owner is determined via README or CODEOWNERS using best effort. In 2026 we will do an EWI to assign owners for unknowns and delete/archive repos that are not in use and have no owners
- description is same as the github repo description.

Note that some repos don't have a circle-ci project associated with them so those repos will get synced onced a week using `catalog-sync-all` worker instead of being synced on every merge.

As long as CI is passing it is safe to merge these PRs but make sure to check that circleci is actually one of the checks because a misconfigured ci file ends up not getting reported instead of reporting an error

This pull request mainly refactors how tool modules are imported and re-exports in the `arc.tools` package, and makes a minor naming correction in the test suite. The most important changes are grouped below:

### Tool import and export organization

* Refactored imports in `src/arc/core/agent.py` to import tool classes directly from their specific submodules (e.g., `arc.tools.bash`, `arc.tools.file_editor`), instead of importing all tools from the top-level `arc.tools` package. This improves clarity and modularity of tool imports.
* Removed re-exports of all tool classes from the `src/arc/tools/__init__.py` file, so only `ToolResult` and `ToolRegistry` are now exported. This reduces the public API surface of the `arc.tools` package and prevents namespace pollution.

### Test suite update

* Renamed `TestMLAgentForTesting` to `MLAgentForTesting` in the test file `tests/core/agents/test_base_agent_ml_tools.py` and updated its usage accordingly, for clearer and more consistent naming. I bought an M4 Mac mini. It enables the ARM64 Branch Target Identification feature, and macOS supports it in kernel mode. Fortunately, this feature is exported to a guest virtual machine, such as QEMU. I installed OpenBSD on the QEMU virtual machine, and the BTI instruction works for me.

I tried supporting the BTI instruction in the same way as the Intel endbr before. The difference between endbr and bti is that bti has 2 variations. The "bti c"  allows landing from an indirect 'call' instruction, and the "bti j" allows landing from an indirect 'jump' instruction.

LuaJIT seems to jump to a generated machine code and to call an assembled code. I inserted "bti j" in the 'emit_endbr' function and "bti c" in the 'vm_arm64.dasc'.

This patch works for LuaJIT-test-cleanup, both testing and benchmarking.

And I also updated 'dasm_arm64.lua' to disassemble the bti instructions.

body:
This commit updates nvim-aider to be compatible with breaking changes introduced in `snacks.nvim` version `v2.24.0`. The previous implementation, which overrode terminal creation, is no longer viable due to new internal assertions in `snacks.nvim`.

The main changes are:
- 🧑‍🔧 Refactor `snacks_ext.lua` to decorate the terminal instance created by `snacks.nvim`'s `Base.open()` instead of replacing it.
- 🩺 Add a version guard in `setup()` and a health check to ensure `snacks.nvim >= v2.24.0` is installed.
- 🎣 Switch from `jobstart` callbacks (`on_stdout`) to `nvim_buf_attach` to detect terminal output, which is more robust with the new API.
- 🧪 Update test mocks to reflect the new `snacks.nvim` behavior.

This ensures nvim-aider continues to function correctly with the latest version of its core dependency.

BREAKING CHANGE: 💥 nvim-aider now requires `snacks.nvim` version `v2.24.0` or newer. The plugin will fail to load if this requirement is not met. Users must update `folke/snacks.nvim` to continue using nvim-aider.

Adds Deepgram as an alternative speech-to-text provider alongside Azure. The issue requested multi-provider support with a common interface to allow switching between providers via configuration.

## Changes

**Domain Layer**
- New `SpeechToTextPort` interface defining the contract for speech-to-text services
- Both Azure and Deepgram adapters implement this interface

**Infrastructure Layer**
- `DeepgramAudioListenerAdapter` - REST API-based implementation with language detection
- `DeepgramSpeechConfig` - Configuration properties for Deepgram
- Refactored `AzureAudioListenerAdapter` to implement `SpeechToTextPort`
- Updated `InfrastructureConfig` with runtime provider selection via `speech.provider` property

**Configuration**
```properties
# Provider selection (azure or deepgram)
speech.provider=deepgram

# Deepgram configuration
deepgram.speech.api-key=${DEEPGRAM_API_KEY}
deepgram.speech.model=nova-2
deepgram.speech.language=es
```

**Usage**
No code changes required to switch providers - configuration only:

```java
@Autowired
private AudioListenerService audioListenerService;

// Works with either provider based on configuration
audioListenerService.listenAudio(audioBean);
```

- 10 new unit tests for Deepgram adapter
- All 149 tests passing
- CodeQL security scan clean

- `DEEPGRAM_INTEGRATION.md` - Technical integration guide
- `USAGE_EXAMPLE.md` - Practical examples and troubleshooting
